claim.supported_scope: Raw-data single-group reflective measurement-only CFA or recursive latent-variable SEM using maximum likelihood and marker-variable identification.
claim.estimand: The ML parameter vector minimizing the normal-theory covariance discrepancy, with supported unstandardized and standardized parameters, residuals, expected-information uncertainty, and bounded fit diagnostics.
assumptions: Input consists of finite listwise-complete continuous observations with a positive-definite sample covariance matrix.
Every latent construct is reflectively measured and marker-identified under the supported CFA or recursive SEM shape.
The optimum converges to a finite admissible solution under the frozen deterministic optimizer contract.
exclusions: Robust ML, ordinal or WLSMV estimation, FIML, formative blocks, interactions, higher-order models, and nonrecursive paths are excluded.
Unrestricted constraints, mean-structure claims, bootstrap publication inference, and unrestricted multigroup invariance are excluded.
Fit statistics do not prove that a model is correct, causal, or uniquely identified.
warnings: Maximum-likelihood inference depends on model identification, distributional assumptions, and admissible convergence.
Modification indices and residual diagnostics are exploratory and must not be treated as automatic model-editing instructions.

equations.expression: F_ml(theta) = log|Sigma(theta)| + trace(S Sigma(theta)^-1) - log|S| - p
Sigma(theta) = Lambda (I - B)^-1 Psi (I - B)^-T Lambda' + Theta

references.citation: Joreskog (1969), A General Approach to Confirmatory Maximum Likelihood Factor Analysis
Bollen (1989), Structural Equations with Latent Variables
Independent Python bounded ML CFA and SEM reference
Development-only lavaan comparison for equivalent supported models

simulations.design: Identified one-, two-, and three-factor CFA plus supported recursive SEM models across sample size, loading strength, path strength, and covariance conditions.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen indexed data-generation seeds by scenario and replicate; deterministic optimization settings are fixed.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Supported scenarios must meet preregistered bias, convergence, admissibility, and independent-reference agreement limits; failed fits remain explicit.

boundaries.case: The sample covariance is singular, non-positive-definite, or contains non-finite values.
boundaries.expected_behavior: The calculation is blocked or fails explicitly without emitting an admissible result.

boundaries.case: The model requests ordinal WLSMV, robust ML, formative blocks, interactions, higher-order constructs, or cycles.
boundaries.expected_behavior: The unsupported request is blocked before estimation.

boundaries.case: Observed and latent variables are consistently reordered with marker assignments preserved.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Mapped parameters, fit values, and residuals remain equal within tolerance.

boundaries.case: The same data, model, and optimizer settings are executed repeatedly.
boundaries.expected_behavior: The analytical CB-SEM payload is exactly equal apart from timestamps.

boundaries.case: A parameter, covariance, fit statistic, method identity, or admissibility flag is changed.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict project validation rejects the archive.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject an archive whose capability identity differs from CB-SEM ML.
Reject a payload relabeled as another CB-SEM estimator version.
Reject a result whose dataset fingerprint differs from saved input.
Reject an archive entry whose checksum differs from the manifest.
Reject duplicate keys, unknown fields, non-finite values, invalid matrix dimensions, or inconsistent parameter identities.
Never reinterpret legacy or preview CB-SEM output as current ML v1 evidence.

persistence.legacy_policy: Historical CB-SEM payloads remain explicitly versioned and cannot satisfy the current promotion contract.

native.gui_cli_parity_rule: GUI and CLI must produce the same parameter, fit, residual, and diagnostic payload for identical data, model, and optimizer settings.
accessibility_rules: Every diagram or matrix has an equivalent accessible table.
Convergence, inadmissibility, warnings, and parameter significance are conveyed without color alone.
